thread.title: Jennifer McClellan advances FirstNet bill and criticizes Trump administration policies
thread.title_full: Jennifer McClellan advances FirstNet bill and criticizes Trump administration policies

author: a. k. lee
title: Jennifer McClellan advances FirstNet bill and criticizes Trump administration policies
text:
Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan, who represents Virginia’s 4th district in the U.S. Congress, announced on March 25, 2026, that her bipartisan bill with Representative Neal Dunn to reauthorize and strengthen the FirstNet emergency communications network has advanced out of committee unanimously and is heading to the House floor for a vote.
In a tweet posted at 20:36 UTC on March 25, McClellan stated: “My bill with @DrNealDunnFL2 to reauthorize and strengthen the FirstNet emergency communications network just advanced out of full committee unanimously! It now heads to the House floor for a vote. The bill will ensure first responders have the tools they need to communicate in a https://t.co/ljAP9U6n1S”.
Shortly after, she invited followers to view her full remarks regarding the legislation by tweeting: “Watch my full remarks here: https://t.co/zdOGARifyJ” at 20:36 UTC.
Later that evening, McClellan criticized former President Donald Trump’s policy priorities in another post. At 22:03 UTC on March 25, she wrote: “Rather than deliver on his campaign promises, Trump prioritizes vanity projects and his mass deportation-detention agenda over the American people. I opposed the Make the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Act as another distraction from this Administration and sought to https://t.co/kzuCDKipJY”.
Jennifer McClellan has represented Virginia’s 4th district since succeeding Donald McEachin in Congress in 2023. Before joining Congress, she served in both chambers of Virginia’s legislature—first as a delegate from 2006 to 2017 and then as a state senator (source). Born in Petersburg in 1972 and currently residing in Richmond, McClellan holds degrees from both the University of Richmond (BA) and University of Virginia (JD).
